简单取放.recommendation: When a put action returns 'Nothing happens', verify current location and navigate to the destination before retrying, rather than repeating the put. Episode 003 shows put failing then succeeding only after go to sofa 1.

Do not self-report failure while a plausible unchecked location remains. In episode 005 the agent declared failure after only two desks, without checking dressers, shelves, beds, or containers where books commonly appear.

Avoid repeated 'go to drawer' commands that return 'Nothing happens'; after one failure, change approach (open the drawer, or move to a different receptacle). Episode 007 looped on drawers and cabinets and never opened most closed cabinets before declaring failure.
Open closed containers before treating them as searched. In episode 007 cabinets 1-4 were approached but never opened, so their contents were never inspected before failure was declared.

When the target is not on the first surfaces, broaden systematically across open surfaces and then containers, tracking checked locations. Episodes 010, 011, 012, and 015 show successful broadening after empty drawers/cabinets to dresser, countertop, or diningtable.
Open a closed destination before placing into it. Episode 023 correctly opened cabinet 1 before putting the soapbottle; this should be the standard for container destinations.

Do not declare failure after exhausting only a narrow set of surfaces; episode 024 checked drawers, one desk, one cabinet, bed, safe, armchairs, and laundryhamper but never opened several closed drawers/cabinets, so the search was incomplete before self-reporting failure.

After acquiring the target, go directly to the destination and place it without intermediate steps. Episodes 002, 004, 014, 016, 019, 021, and 022 show the clean acquire-then-place pattern succeeding in few steps.

台灯观察.recommendation: When the target object is already visible on the same surface as the desklamp, take it first and then use the numbered lamp; do not call use desklamp before holding the target, since that can return 'Nothing happens' and waste steps.

If use desklamp returns 'Nothing happens', verify the lamp is actually present at the current furniture; the observation may list no desklamp there. Then move to the furniture where a desklamp was observed rather than retrying the same use command.

Do not declare completion merely because the lamp was turned on. Confirm the goal predicate from the observation; if the environment does not confirm the observation, continue with a valid action such as taking the target while at the lamp.

Avoid unsupported actions like 'look at X' or bare 'look' when searching; use go to a receptacle and read its listed contents. If a location shows no desklamp, move to another plausible surface instead of issuing examine/look commands.

When the target object is not at the first checked surface, broaden systematically across plausible open surfaces (beds, dressers, sidetables, sofas, coffeetables) before opening many drawers; this finds targets faster and avoids long empty drawer sweeps.

After acquiring the target, go directly to the furniture carrying the observed desklamp and use the numbered lamp instance; do not add intermediate placements or extra navigation once the target is held.
If a navigation target such as a nonexistent drawer returns 'Nothing happens', treat it as unavailable and switch to a known valid location rather than continuing to enumerate invalid targets.

When both the target and desklamp are visible on the same surface, the efficient sequence is take the target then use the numbered lamp; this pattern succeeded repeatedly and should be preferred over using the lamp before acquisition.

清洗后放置.recommendation: When the goal names a specific object type (e.g., 'knife', 'cup'), do not substitute a similar subtype such as butterknife or mug unless the observation explicitly treats it as equivalent. In episode_052 the agent took butterknife 1 for a 'knife' goal and in episode_060 took mug 2 for a 'cup' goal; both ended in executor/environment errors. Search for the exact named type first.

Do not attempt to clean an object type that may not support cleaning (e.g., towel/cloth). In episode_049 'clean towel 1 with sinkbasin 1' returned 'Nothing happens', and the agent then looped on failed takes and puts until budget exhaustion. After a failed clean, reassess whether the chosen object is cleanable and switch candidates rather than continuing to manipulate it.

After a failed take or put, change at least one condition instead of repeating the identical command. In episode_049 the agent issued 'take cloth 1 from cabinet 2' three times and 'put towel 1' at multiple invalid receptacles, all returning 'Nothing happens'. Verify location, container open state, and held-object state before retrying.

When a destination container's open action returns 'Nothing happens', treat it as already open or non-openable and proceed directly to put rather than retrying open. In episode_055 'open cabinet 1' returned 'Nothing happens' and the subsequent put succeeded; in episode_052 the agent put into drawer 1 without opening it and succeeded. Do not loop on open.

Maintain a checked-location record and avoid revisiting confirmed-empty surfaces. In episode_063 the agent returned to countertop 1 after already checking it, then opened many cabinets and drawers before declaring failure; in episode_044 a 'go to drawer 5' returned 'Nothing happens' yet the agent continued. Track visited locations and move to new plausible ones.

Follow the clean-then-place order strictly: acquire, clean at sinkbasin, confirm the clean observation, then go to destination and place. Successful episodes (043, 044, 045, 046, 047, 048, 050, 051, 053, 054, 056, 057, 058, 059, 061, 062, 064, 065, 066, 067, 069, 070, 071, 073) all show this sequence with an explicit clean confirmation before placement. Do not place before cleaning.

Search visible surfaces first and broaden to containers only when needed. Successful episodes found targets on countertops, diningtables, shelves, or in the fridge quickly (e.g., 045 cup on countertop, 046 bowl on diningtable, 062 soapbar on shelf 4). When the first surface is empty, move to a new plausible location rather than re-checking the same one.

Declare completion only after the placement observation confirms the goal, and do not emit an extra empty action afterward. In episode_052 and episode_060 the agent emitted a final empty action with 'Status: COMPLETED' after a confirmed put, which coincided with executor/environment errors. Treat the confirming put observation as terminal and stop.

加热后放置.recommendation: When heating fails with 'Nothing happens' while holding the object at an open microwave, place the object inside the open microwave and retry; if that also fails, take it out and retry while holding. Do not repeat the identical failing heat command. Episode 087 shows three identical failures before the position change succeeded.

Do not substitute a different object type for the goal object. In episode 081 the goal was a cup but a mug was taken and heated; the run failed. Search for the exact named type (cup vs mug) before committing.

After a confirmed placement, stop. Do not issue extra take/put/cool cycles. Episode 093 placed the mug in the coffeemachine, then repeatedly took it out, tried cooling, and re-placed it, ending in failure. Treat the confirming put observation as terminal.

When a take from a container returns 'Nothing happens' (e.g., taking a mug from the microwave that was never placed there), do not retry the same take. Verify inventory/held state and proceed. Episode 090 repeated a failed take twice before recovering.

Search visible surfaces before opening many closed containers. Episodes 075 and 088 spent many steps opening cabinets before finding the mug; prioritizing countertops, tables, and shelves first would reduce wasted actions.
Open the microwave before attempting heat; a heat issued while the microwave is closed returns 'Nothing happens'. Episode 087 issued heat before opening and wasted a step.

After heating succeeds while holding the object, go directly to the destination and place it; do not add intermediate placements or re-take from the microwave. Episodes 074, 076, and 083 show the clean acquire-heat-place sequence that succeeds.

If the destination container is closed, open it before putting; if open returns no effect, proceed without retrying. Episodes 077, 080, and 084 correctly opened the destination before placing the heated object.

冷却后放置.recommendation: When the target object is not found after checking the fridge, countertops, and a few cabinets, avoid opening every remaining cabinet one by one. Track checked locations and reassess feasibility earlier, since exhaustive cabinet sweeps consumed the action budget in failed episodes.

After a 'go to cabinet N' returns 'Nothing happens', do not repeat the identical command. Treat that identifier as unreachable and move to a different cabinet or location, as repeated identical go attempts wasted steps in several episodes.

The reliable cooling pattern is: acquire the exact target, go to the fridge, open it, then issue 'cool <object> with fridge <id>' while holding the object, and only proceed after the cooled confirmation. This sequence succeeded consistently across many episodes.

After cooling, go directly to the destination, open it if closed, and put the object. Do not add intermediate placements or re-take an already-held object; the cooled object remains in inventory after the cool action.

When the goal names a specific object type (e.g., cup), do not silently substitute a similar object (e.g., mug) unless the environment treats them as equivalent. Episode 102 took a mug for a 'cup' goal and ended in error; prefer searching for the exact named type or confirming equivalence.

Before declaring failure, ensure all plausible open surfaces and relevant containers were actually inspected, not merely approached. In episode 100 the agent declared failure after opening only some cabinets while many remained unchecked; a bounded but complete search of likely locations should precede a failure report.

Search visible surfaces first (countertops, dining tables) before opening closed containers, and stop revisiting surfaces already confirmed empty. Episode 106 revisited countertop 2 and swept many cabinets without tracking, exhausting the budget.

If a destination cabinet returns 'Nothing happens' on open or put, switch to a different valid cabinet rather than retrying the same one. Episode 116 recovered by moving to cabinet 4 after cabinets 1-3 failed, then placed successfully.

双物品放置.recommendation: When a put into the final destination returns 'Nothing happens', do not assume the object was placed. Verify by navigating to the destination and retrying the put there; only then start the second search cycle. In episode 118 the first soapbottle put into toilet failed and was never confirmed, yet the agent proceeded to search for the second item.

If the destination receptacle rejects placement (e.g., toilet returns 'Nothing happens' for a soapbottle), treat it as an invalid destination rather than retrying the same put. Reassess whether the named destination is reachable/valid and report blocked instead of looping or abandoning the held object.

When holding an object and a put fails, do not keep trying unrelated receptacles (sinkbasin, toilet, garbagecan, drawers) to free hands. Prefer placing directly into the final destination; if that is impossible, choose one open stable surface and confirm success before continuing. Episode 123 exhausted the budget repeatedly failing puts while holding a towel.

Do not attempt to take a second object while already holding one; the take returns 'Nothing happens'. Immediately navigate to the destination and place the held object, then return for the second. This recovery worked in episodes 122, 124, 125, and 131.

A put issued before reaching the destination returns 'Nothing happens'. Navigate to the destination first, then put. Episode 124 step 4 failed because the put was issued while still at the sofa; after going to armchair 1 the put succeeded.

Do not declare failure while still holding an unplaced object or before checking all plausible locations. In episode 126 the agent held candle 1, never placed it, and self-reported failure after checking only cabinets and one garbagecan; it should have placed the held candle and continued searching surfaces.

Track checked locations and avoid revisiting confirmed-empty surfaces. In episode 133 the agent re-checked coffeetable 1 and armchair 2 after already confirming them empty, then stalled without finding the second creditcard; maintain a checked-location list and prioritize unchecked containers.

When a go-to returns 'Nothing happens' (e.g., towelholder 2 in episode 123), treat that target as unreachable and switch to another candidate rather than repeating it. Also avoid opening non-container surfaces like shelves, which returns no effect.

简单取放.recommendation: When a put returns 'Nothing happens', the Critic should direct the Executor to navigate to the destination first and then retry the put, rather than repeating the put in place. Episode 003 shows the correct recovery: failed put, go to sofa 1, then successful put.

When a go-to returns 'Nothing happens' for a drawer or cabinet, treat that target as unreachable and switch to a different unchecked location instead of retrying the same identifier. Episode 007 and 009 show repeated failed go-to drawer commands wasting steps before moving on.

When a closed container is reached, the Critic should explicitly advise opening it before inspecting or taking, and should not accept a bare go-to as a search of that container. Episodes 010, 013, and 017 show closed drawers/cabinets needing an open action before contents are known.

After several empty closed containers, the Critic should recommend broadening to open surfaces such as countertops, dining tables, dressers, and sidetables rather than continuing through more cabinets. Episodes 011 and 015 succeed only after shifting from cabinets/drawers to countertop and diningtable.

The Critic should confirm acquisition from the observation before advising movement to the destination, and should not treat arriving at a location containing the target as acquisition. Episode 008 shows the Critic correctly noting that being at desk 1 without taking a CD leaves the goal unmet.

When the Executor self-reports failure after only a few locations, the Critic should check whether plausible open surfaces and containers were actually opened and inspected before accepting failure. Episodes 005 and 024 end in self-reported failure with limited coverage of likely locations.

The Critic should avoid recommending redundant navigation to a location already reached, and should instead advise the next productive action such as open, take, or put. Episode 017 shows a redundant go-to drawer 4 after already being there.

For simple pick-and-place, the Critic's advice should stay within the two-stage acquire-then-place frame and stop once the placement observation confirms success, without adding verification steps. Episodes 002, 004, and 019 complete cleanly with take-then-put and no extra actions.

台灯观察.recommendation: When the target object is already visible on the same surface as the desklamp, take it and immediately use the numbered desklamp without extra navigation. Episodes 027 and 036 show this succeeds in 2-3 steps; avoid detours to unrelated furniture.

When the desklamp is not on the first assumed surface, do not conclude it is absent; continue to other surfaces. Episode 029's use desklamp failed at desk 1, then succeeded after finding desklamp 1 on sidetable 1. Episode 040 similarly found the lamp on sidetable 2.

After a failed use desklamp, change location or object state rather than repeating the same command. Episode 041 issued use desklamp twice with no effect, then recovered only after moving the bowl to shelf 1 where a desklamp was present and using it there.

Do not declare failure merely because the target object is absent from the first surface. Episodes 032 and 033 self-reported failure after only one or two locations, while other episodes succeeded by continuing to search beds, dressers, shelves, and sidetables.

When the target is not at the desklamp surface, acquire it first and carry it to the lamp. Episodes 026, 028, 030, 034, 039, 042 all succeeded by taking the object elsewhere then navigating to the desklamp and using it.

Avoid long drawer-by-drawer sweeps before checking open surfaces. Episode 025 opened/checked many drawers with no newspaper before finding it on the sofa; prioritize visible surfaces like sofas, beds, and tables first.

Do not issue go to on an invalid or unreachable target; episode 037's go to drawer 8 returned Nothing happens. Verify reachable locations and switch to a known location such as the desklamp surface instead of retrying.

Use the numbered lamp instance (use desklamp 1) and avoid examine-style or bare-name variants. Episode 041's examine bowl 1 returned Nothing happens, while numbered use desklamp succeeded in all successful episodes.

清洗后放置.recommendation: When a clean-then-place goal names a specific object type (e.g., 'cloth', 'cup', 'knife'), do not substitute a similar item like a towel or mug. In episode_049 the executor took a towel for a 'cloth' goal and could not clean it; in episode_052 it took a butterknife for a 'knife' goal. Search for the exact named type and only use a confirmed equivalent.

If a clean action returns 'Nothing happens' after confirming the object is held at a sinkbasin, treat the object as likely non-cleanable and stop repeating clean. In episode_049 the towel failed to clean and the executor then looped on take/put attempts instead of switching to a cleanable candidate or reporting blocked.

When a put fails with 'Nothing happens', verify the destination is a valid open receptacle and that the object is actually held before retrying. In episode_049 repeated put attempts on sinkbasin, countertop, and bathtubbasin all failed while the towel was still held, and the executor never freed its hands to acquire the cloth.

Before placing into a closed container, open it first; if open returns no effect, treat it as already open or non-openable and proceed. In episode_052 the executor put the butterknife into a closed drawer without opening it, and in episode_055 open cabinet 1 returned 'Nothing happens' yet placement still succeeded.

After arriving at the sinkbasin with the target held, immediately issue the clean command rather than pausing or moving on. In episode_043 and episode_055 the critic noted the executor reached the sinkbasin but had not yet cleaned, requiring an explicit prompt to clean before placement.

Bound the search for the target object: after checking a reasonable set of likely surfaces and containers, reassess or report blocked rather than opening every remaining cabinet/drawer. In episode_063 the executor exhausted many cabinets and drawers without finding the kettle and self-reported failure; in episode_044 it checked many drawers before finding the kettle on a stoveburner.

When a go-to action returns 'Nothing happens' (e.g., an unreachable drawer), do not repeat it; switch to another plausible unchecked location. In episode_044 'go to drawer 5' and in episode_053 'go to drawer 4' returned no effect, and the executor correctly moved on to other locations.

Confirm the clean state from the observation before moving to the destination, and confirm placement before declaring success. Successful episodes (e.g., episode_045, episode_046, episode_048) show clean then put with explicit confirmation; the critic should flag any move to destination that occurs before a clean-success observation.

加热后放置.recommendation: When heating while holding returns 'Nothing happens', the recovery is to place the object into the open microwave, then take it back out and heat while holding—not to keep retrying the identical heat command. Episodes 082, 087, 090, 095, 096 all succeeded only after this put-then-take-then-heat cycle. Critic should explicitly recommend this state change after the first failed heat.

Critic repeatedly advised opening a closed microwave before heating, which is correct, but in episodes 087 and 090 the executor issued heat commands before opening and got 'Nothing happens'. Critic should flag the ordering violation explicitly: verify the microwave is open (observation says 'is open') before endorsing any heat action, rather than only noting it after the fact.

In episode 093 the Critic endorsed switching to a stoveburner after microwave heating failed, then later endorsed placing an unheated mug in the coffeemachine and even a 'cool' action—none of which satisfied the hot-mug goal, and the episode failed. Critic should not recommend blind appliance substitution or accept placement without confirmed heating; instead insist on correcting the microwave interaction (open, put in, take out, heat) and treat unconfirmed heat as failure.

In episode 090 the Critic misdiagnosed the failure as 'microwave occupied by a mug' and advised removing the mug, but the real issue was heating while holding. Critic should base diagnosis on the actual observation (object held, microwave open) rather than inventing an occupancy conflict, and recommend the put-take-heat recovery.

In long searches (episodes 075, 079, 088, 093) the Critic correctly pushed to open closed cabinets, but also sometimes advised broadening to 'countertops or drawers' after cabinets were already being checked, and in 093 the search ran ~40 steps before finding the mug. Critic should maintain a checked-location record and direct the executor to unchecked opened containers and visible surfaces, avoiding redundant revisits and premature broadening.

In episode 079 the Critic advised broadening to 'countertops or drawers' after cabinet 5 was empty, but the plate was eventually found on a diningtable. Critic should prioritize open surfaces (diningtable, countertop, sidetable) alongside containers when the object type is a dish, rather than steering only toward more cabinets/drawers.

In episode 088 the Critic noted shelf 2 lacked a mug and advised checking cabinets/drawers, but the mug was in cabinet 7 and the executor had to open many cabinets. Critic should confirm each cabinet is actually opened and inspected (not merely approached) before moving on, and track which were opened empty versus unopened.

Across successful episodes (074, 076, 077, 078, 080, 083, 084, 085, 086, 089, 091, 092, 094) the Critic's guidance to open the microwave before heating and then proceed directly to the destination was effective. Critic should keep this concise pattern: confirm heat success from the observation, then direct a single go-to-destination and put, without adding intermediate placements.

冷却后放置.recommendation: When the target object is not found after checking many cabinets/drawers, stop opening more containers and reassess: revisit visible surfaces (countertops, stoveburners, dining tables) and consider the object may be absent. In episode_114 the pan was never found and the budget was exhausted; in episode_106 the tomato search looped through cabinets until timeout. Track checked locations and escalate early rather than continuing blind exhaustive checks.

Do not repeat an identical failed navigation or open command. In episode_100 'go to cabinet 2' returned Nothing happens twice in a row; in episode_104 and episode_106 the same no-op navigation was retried. After one no-change result, switch to a different reachable location or verify the identifier instead of reissuing the same command.

Cooling is reliably done by holding the object at an open fridge and issuing an explicit cool action, then confirming the 'You cool ...' observation before moving on. Successful episodes 097, 098, 099, 101, 105, 107, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112, 113, 115, 116, 117 all follow this pattern. Do not treat mere containment in the fridge as cooling.

After cooling, go directly to the destination, open it if closed, and put the object; confirm the put observation. Episodes 097, 098, 103, 111, 115 show open-then-put at the destination. Do not insert intermediate placements or re-take an already-held object.

When a destination cabinet open returns Nothing happens (episode_116), do not loop on open; treat it as already open or non-openable and attempt the put at a valid destination. The successful recovery was to navigate to another cabinet and put there. Avoid repeating open on the same cabinet.

Search should prioritize visible open surfaces before opening many closed containers. In episode_101 the potato was found on countertop 1 immediately; in episode_099 the bowl was on countertop 2. When the object is not on the first surface, broaden systematically across countertops, dining tables, stoveburners, then containers, rather than opening cabinet after cabinet.

Match the exact object type named in the goal. Episode_102's goal was 'cool cup' but the agent took and placed a mug; episode_098's goal was 'pot' and it correctly took pot 1. Do not silently substitute a similar object (mug for cup) unless the environment confirms equivalence.

Declare success only after the final put observation confirms the object is at the destination. Episodes 097, 098, 105, 107, 110, 112, 113, 117 end with a confirming put. Do not stop after cooling or after opening the destination; the cooled state and placement are separate checkpoints.

双物品放置.recommendation: When a put into the final destination returns 'Nothing happens', the Critic should first check whether the Executor is actually at the destination before suggesting an alternative receptacle. In episode 118 the Critic wrongly concluded toilets reject placement and advised switching to sinkbasin/bathtubbasin, but the real cause was not being at the toilet; the correct advice is to navigate to the destination and retry the put.

When a take fails while an object is already held, the Critic should diagnose the one-item carry limit and advise placing the held object at the final destination before taking the second. Episode 121 shows this diagnosis working; episodes 128 and 131 show the same pattern where the Critic should consistently attribute the failed second take to occupied inventory rather than to the object being absent.

When a go-to returns 'Nothing happens', the Critic should not advise re-issuing the same navigation. In episode 131 the Critic told the Executor to verify location and retry handtowelholder 2, which repeated the no-op; instead advise that the Executor is likely already at that location and should proceed to the next action (take or put) rather than re-navigating.

The Critic should avoid asserting that a placement succeeded when the observation shows 'Nothing happens'. In episode 133 the Critic claimed the first creditcard was placed in armchair 1, but the put had failed and the object was still held, leading the Executor to search for a second card while encumbered. Verify placement from the observation before declaring a cycle complete.

When the Executor is stuck holding an object and every put attempt returns 'Nothing happens' across many receptacles (episode 123), the Critic should stop suggesting yet another receptacle and instead reassess: confirm the held object's exact identifier and whether the destination surface accepts placement, and consider that the object may be unplaceable or the goal infeasible rather than looping through sinkbasin, toilet, garbagecan, etc.

When a closed container is reached, the Critic should advise opening it before inspecting or taking, and when an open action returns 'Nothing happens' on an already-open or non-openable fixture, advise proceeding rather than reopening. Episode 127 shows correct open-before-inspect advice; episode 118 shows the Critic misattributing a failed open to being at the wrong position when the container was simply not the right target.

After several empty containers, the Critic should steer the Executor toward visible open surfaces (countertops, tables, shelves) rather than continuing to open more cabinets/drawers. Episodes 127, 129, and 134 show this broadening advice being effective; the Critic should apply it consistently once a few closed containers are confirmed empty.

When the Executor has just navigated to the destination while holding the first object, the Critic should give the single next action (put the held object now) rather than a multi-step plan. Episodes 122, 125, and 127 show this concise 'place the held object now' advice working; keep recommendations to one concrete next step to avoid confusing the Executor.

skill.title: 台灯观察：先取得目标物，再到台灯所在家具使用带编号台灯
skill.principle: 先确认目标物和台灯位置；台灯通常固定在家具表面。若目标物与台灯在同一表面被观察到，先 take 目标物，再使用带实例编号的 use desklamp <id>；不要在未持有目标物时先 use desklamp，否则常返回 Nothing happens。若目标物不在台灯处，先取得并携带目标物到承载台灯的家具。到达后使用 use desklamp <id> 触发观察；不要用裸名或复合语法，也不要把台灯当作可携带物或导航点。
skill.when_to_apply: 当任务要求 examine/look at 某物 with/under the desklamp，且环境中存在可交互的 desklamp 时。

skill.description: 如果 use desklamp 返回 Nothing happens，通常说明当前不在台灯所在位置、当前家具观察中并无台灯，或交互条件未满足；同一位置重复同一 use/examine/look 指令不会改变状态，并可能形成循环或触发保护。连续一两次失败后应停止重复。
skill.why_it_happens: 使用台灯要求与台灯所在家具同处，且错误语法或位置不会产生状态变化；把空观察误当作可重试信号会重复无效动作。
skill.how_to_avoid: 失败后先核对当前家具观察中是否确实列出 desklamp；若没有，移动到已观察到台灯的其他家具，而不是重试同一 use。若台灯在场，确保目标物已取得或保持后改用带编号 use desklamp <id> 重试；若仍无变化，改为搜索其他位置或声明无法完成，不要重复相同指令。

skill.title: 台灯观察搜索策略：优先开放表面并系统检查容器
skill.principle: 搜索目标物或台灯时，优先检查与台灯相关的开放表面，如 desk、sidetable、床头柜、床、dresser、sofa、coffeetable 等；一旦观察到台灯，应直接前往其所在家具并在需要时使用台灯，不要继续遍历大量抽屉。若合理开放表面没有目标物，再按容器类型（drawer/cabinet）系统搜索，找到后返回台灯处。避免反复 look/examine 同一位置；没有新信息时转向其他家具或容器。'under the desklamp' 不保证目标物或台灯一定在假定位置，因此假定位置不可见时应搜索其他表面和容器。
skill.when_to_apply: 在台灯观察任务中寻找目标物或台灯，或已到达假定台灯位置但目标物或台灯不在该处、连续观察无新信息时。

skill.description: Placement can fail when the destination container is closed, has no available space, or is not a valid receptacle; for example, some fixtures such as toilets or coffeemachines may reject placement. An open action may also return no effect if the container is already open or not openable.
skill.why_it_happens: Containers may require opening or have capacity limits; some fixtures are not valid placement targets. Repeating put or open without changing conditions may waste steps.
skill.how_to_avoid: Before placing, open a closed destination; if open returns no effect, treat it as already open or non-openable and proceed directly to put rather than retrying open. Check for space or availability when possible. If the destination is invalid or put repeatedly has no effect, seek an alternative valid destination or report blocked rather than looping.

skill.title: Microwave heating with observation-driven holding/placement recovery
skill.principle: Open the microwave before taking from or using it. Observations conflict on the required heating state: some successful runs heated the object while holding it, while others succeeded by placing the object in an open microwave and then heating. Treat the holding/placement requirement as observation-dependent. If heating while holding returns 'Nothing happens', place the object in the open microwave and retry. If heating with the object inside returns 'Nothing happens', take it out, ensure the microwave is open, and retry while holding it. Use the exact supported form heat <object> with microwave <id>; do not issue use <object> or heat <appliance>. Do not repeat an identical failing heat command without changing the object's position or holding state.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target object must be heated with a microwave, especially if the first heat attempt fails or the object is inside the microwave.

skill.title: Cooling workflow with confirmed cool state before placement
skill.principle: Inputs differ on whether cooling requires placing the object in the fridge and taking it out or issuing an explicit cool action while holding it at an open fridge. Use environment feedback as authority: perform or verify cooling explicitly, and do not treat mere containment or brief placement as confirmed cooling. A reliable sequence is: acquire the exact target; go to the fridge; open it; while holding the object at the open fridge issue cool <object> with fridge <id> and wait for a cooled-state confirmation; then go to the destination; open it if closed; put the object there; confirm placement. Do not immediately re-take an object already held; check inventory before re-taking.
